questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

A good lawyer / always looks in the / case before he / attends court.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**looks in the**" is grammatically incorrect in the given context.
 
• The correct phrasal verb is "**looks into the case**", which means to examine or investigate the case carefully.
 
• "Look in" refers to briefly visiting a place, which does not fit the meaning of a lawyer preparing for a case.
 
• Therefore, the error lies in **part 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"A good lawyer always looks into the case before he attends court."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1) attends court** – This is grammatically correct. "Attend court" is a common collocation in legal contexts.
 
• **3) case before he** – This phrase is contextually and grammatically accurate.
 
• **4) A good lawyer** – This phrase is correct and serves as the proper subject of the sentence.

• The idiom **"On the back foot"** means being in a disadvantaged or defensive position. (असुविधाजनक स्थिति में)

• Hence, the idiom "On the back foot" aligns with the meaning "At a disadvantage."

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

According to Greek mythology, Sipylus is __holier__ city of Lydia.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The adjective "**holier**" is the comparative degree, used when comparing two entities.
 
• However, the sentence implies a superlative degree — Sipylus is being referred to as the most sacred among all cities in Lydia.
 
• Therefore, the correct form should be "**the holiest**," which is the superlative form of "holy."
 
• Using "**most holiest**" is grammatically incorrect because it involves a double comparison (redundancy).

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"According to Greek mythology, Sipylus is **the holiest** city of Lydia."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 – "most holiest"** is incorrect because "holiest" is already in the superlative form; adding "most" makes it redundant.
 
• **Option 3 – "the holier"** is a comparative form used for comparing two things, not suitable here.
 
• **Option 4 – "most holy"** is acceptable but less concise than "the holiest"; "holiest" is the grammatically preferred superlative form of "holy."

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Before the internet was available on mobile, I read often books for entertainment and information.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**I read often books**" is incorrect due to improper adverb placement.
 
• In English grammar, the adverb "**often**" should typically be placed **before the main verb** but after the subject — especially in simple tenses.
 
• The correct structure should be: "**I often read books**."
 
• Thus, the error lies in the positioning of the word "**often**" in Option 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Before the internet was available on mobile, I **often read books** for entertainment and information."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 – "for entertainment and information"** is grammatically correct and meaningful.
 
• **Option 2 – "was available on mobile"** is correctly phrased to describe the medium (mobile).
 
• **Option 3 – "Before the internet"** correctly introduces the subordinate clause referring to a past time period.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical/spelling error.

They decided to / start their journey / towards the hills / in midnight.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**in midnight**" is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct preposition to use with "midnight" is "**at**," not "in."
 
• "At" is used with specific points of time (e.g., **at noon**, **at night**, **at midnight**), whereas "in" is used for longer periods like months or years.
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase should be "**at midnight**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"They decided to start their journey towards the hills **at midnight**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 – "They decided to"** is grammatically correct and complete.
 
• **Option 2 – "start their journey"** is a correct phrase indicating the beginning of an action.
 
• **Option 4 – "towards the hills"** correctly shows direction and is appropriate in the context.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate superlative adjective form to fill in the blanks.

What's ___ book you've ever read?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**the most interesting**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The question uses the phrase "**you've ever read**", indicating a comparison among all the books read so far.
 
• This requires the **superlative** form of the adjective "interesting".
 
• The correct superlative form is "**the most interesting**", as "interesting" is a multi-syllable adjective and forms its comparative/superlative with "more" and "most".
 
• Options like "**more interesting**" are comparative, not superlative, and "**the interesting**" is grammatically incorrect in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"What's **the most interesting**__ book you've ever read?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "interesting"** is incorrect as it lacks the necessary comparison or emphasis.
 
• **Option 3: "more interesting"** is a comparative adjective, used when comparing two things—not suitable here.
 
• **Option 4: "the interesting"** is grammatically incorrect as it lacks a proper noun to follow and is not a superlative form.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate present tense form of the verb to fill in the blank.

________ they like sweets?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Do**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject "**they**" is a **plural pronoun**.
 
• In the **present simple tense**, the correct auxiliary verb used with plural subjects is "**do**".
 
• "Does" is used for singular third-person subjects (e.g., he, she, it).
 
• "Had" is past tense and not suitable here, and "has" is used for possession, not for forming questions in the present tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"**Do**__ they like sweets?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "Had"** is past perfect tense, incorrect in a present tense question.
 
• **Option 3: "Has"** is used for possession and with singular subjects (e.g., he has, she has).
 
• **Option 4: "Does"** is incorrect here because it is used with singular third-person subjects only.

Despite his initial ________, he eventually agreed to join the team.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**reluctance**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses the word "**Despite**," indicating contrast between the initial feeling and the final action.
 
• "**Reluctance**" means unwillingness or hesitation to do something, which fits logically with someone eventually agreeing despite initial hesitation.
 
• The phrase "**he eventually agreed**" confirms that his initial state was contrary, hence "reluctance" is appropriate.
 
• Other options like "**enthusiasm**", "**determination**", and "**compassion**" do not create the required contrast.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Despite his initial **reluctance**__, he eventually agreed to join the team.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Enthusiasm (उत्साह)**: intense interest or eagerness—opposite in meaning to what's implied here.
 
• **Determination (दृढ़ संकल्प)**: firmness of purpose—not showing hesitation.
 
• **Compassion (दया)**: sympathy or concern for others—unrelated to willingness or agreement.

• The verb "**earn**" appropriately fits the context of receiving income or sustenance through work or industrial opportunities.
 
• Other verbs such as "**live**", "**give**", or "**break**" do not logically or grammatically fit in this phrase.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Industrialisation gives even the least talented person a chance to **earn**__ his livelihood.*

**Complete Sentence:** *The investigating team smelled a **rat**__ in the suspect's defence.*

__
 
• The verb "**refers**" is commonly followed by the preposition "**to**" in standard English usage.
 
• The phrase "**refers to**" means "to mention" or "to be about" something, which fits the context of introducing the definition of opera.
 
• Other prepositions like "**on**", "**for**", and "**with**" are grammatically incorrect after "refers" in this context.
 
• Hence, the appropriate phrase is "**Opera refers to** a dramatic art form..."

Complete Sentence: *Opera refers to__ a dramatic art form, originating in Europe, in which the emotional content is conveyed to the audience...*

• **With**: Indicates association or instrumentality—e.g., "He came with his friend."

__
 
• The subject "**emotional content**" is singular, so it requires a singular verb.
 
• The correct verb form in present tense for a singular subject is "**is**".
 
• The sentence is describing a general truth about opera, so the **simple present tense** is appropriate.

• **Are**: Present tense but plural, incorrect for the singular subject "content".
 
• **Are being**: Present continuous passive, implies ongoing action, which doesn't fit the general truth being stated.
